statement: The function returns a result r, and r equals the maximum, over all arrays perm of length len(nums) that are rearrangements of nums (that is, for every integer value v, the number of indices i with perm[i] = v equals the number of indices i with nums[i] = v), of the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and perm[i] > nums[i].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r and does not fail with overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let m be the maximum, over all integer values v, of the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= len(nums) - m.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let m be the maximum, over all integer values v, of the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v. Whenever the function returns a result r, len(nums) - m <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists an array perm of length len(nums) that is a rearrangement of nums and such that exactly r indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) satisfy perm[i] > nums[i].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: If the function returns r on nums and returns r2 on nums2, then r = r2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; nums2 is an array of the same length such that for every integer value v, the number of indices i with nums2[i] = v equals the number of indices i with nums[i] = v.
